## CHAPTER SIX & THE LAST

->*How the operation is to be established.*<-

If all these aforementioned things have finally been duly prepared and are ready at hand, and the operator has sufficiently tested and prepared himself to be suitable (just as this work requires an altogether undaunted and high-spirited man), let him approach at the same often-indicated time, hour, and night of **Venus** <term>♀</term> a place secure from all disturbance of people—either in a house or, better yet, in the forests and remote, deserted crossroads. Let him arrange a circle <term>circulum</term> there, and hang the Seal <term>Sigillum</term> of **Venus** <term>♀</term> around his neck, perform the fumigation <term>fumigium</term>, and begin to summon the spirit <term>Spiritum</term> chosen from the number he has selected.

Let him pronounce the entire calling through the **Trumpet of Venus** <term>♀</term> <note>This refers to the "libellus" or consecrated book described on the previous page, which was named "The Trumpet of Venus"</note>; let him call the Spirit by its name both at the beginning of the citation and at the end, but always with a certain pause.

*Let the practitioner greet the arriving Spirit in the following manner.*

Hail, noble and obedient Spirit (*name the Spirit here by its own name*), I command you by the awesome <note>original: "tremendum," meaning a name to be feared or trembled at</note> name of Adonai <note>A Hebrew name for God, frequently used in Western magical traditions for its perceived power</note>, and by this Sigil <note>A mystical seal or signature unique to a specific spirit</note> (*show the Spirit the Sigil of the angel Anael, the ruling prince of the planet Venus*) that you show yourself quiet and peaceful, and that in all things which I shall command you, you fulfill my will. This I command you again by God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and by the triumphant Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the world by fire.

After this, the Spirit will ask the master: why has he been summoned, and what does the master command and desire? The master should declare this clearly and distinctly.

Where it must be noted: if the Spirits should show themselves stubborn in any way, let the Sigil of <term>Venus</term> <note>Represented by the symbol ♀ in the original text</note> be taken and placed over the fire, or the coals with which the incense <note>original: "fumigium," refers to ritual smoke or fumigation</note> was made; or if incense is not used (*as it is not strictly necessary*), let the Sigil be held over a burning candle until it becomes hot, and the Sigil of that Spirit which is being summoned should be placed upon it. For by this means the Spirits are enormously tortured, and they will beg the master to cease tormenting them, and they will no longer resist fulfilling his will.

However, I would advise that the master <note>original: "magister," referring to the ritual practitioner</note> should not exceed too much in his requests and desires, lest perhaps he provoke the wrath of the Divine Deity; nor should he show himself inconsistent or wavering to the cunning spirits; nor should he accept conditions proposed by them; but with a brave and constant spirit, he should insist on the requests once proposed by him to the spirits, and he should value the perhaps simultaneous difficulties or even threats of the Spirits as being worth a straw <note>original: "nauci floccique," a Latin idiom meaning of no value or significance, literally "a nut-shell and a tuft of wool"</note>; otherwise, he would be frustrated in his mastery over the Spirits.

No less must care be taken, lest he use the assistance of the Spirits for perpetrating impious and wicked crimes; toward which, indeed, the Spirits show themselves all the more ready.

Truly, the soul would certainly suffer the greatest harm, for while he would wish to exercise his dominion over demons <note>original: "dæmones"</note>: he would also deliver his soul into a horrendous bondage <note>original: "mancipatum," a legal term for a formal transfer of property or slavery</note>.

Therefore, in a few words, we faithfully discourage all and each from every abuse of the art. If, therefore, the Spirits have fulfilled the commands or the will of the master, they should be dismissed in the following manner.

->*What further things must yet be observed in the operation.*<-

If the experiment is performed with companions, only the one acting as the Master and summoning them shall speak to the spirits; all others must maintain silence.

If the Spirits are compelled to bring treasures and coins, the <term>Seal of Venus</term> <note>The original uses the symbol ♀ for Venus. Afterward, the treasure should be emptied from its containers and transferred into another new container that has been previously perfumed <note>original: "perfumatum," referring to ritual purification with incense</note> and blessed. With these instructions, therefore, we bring our little book <note>original: "libello," a term for a small book or manual</note> to its conclusion.

But you, friend reader! Beware of the abuse of this knowledge. Weigh well what is written here; take care that you forget nothing; and whatever you do, act prudently. Complete your work with an undaunted and constant spirit, and it will bring you great benefit and comfort.

# How to make these seals of the spirits.

One should take green wax mixed with lampblack <note>original: "Kienruß" — a fine black pigment collected from the soot of burnt resinous wood, used here to color the ritual wax.</note>, make small round tablets from it, and with a steel stylus, scratch the <term>seal</term> <note>A "sigill" or seal is a unique geometric symbol representing a specific spirit, acting as a "signature" or focal point for the magician's intent.</note> of whichever spirit one intends to summon. This must occur during the same days and hours of <term>Venus</term> <note>Planetary hours are a system of timekeeping in magic where each hour of the day is ruled by a planet; Venusian hours (usually on Fridays) are chosen for spirits associated with her sphere of influence.</note>, and in the very same manner as everything described previously. ## How to Find the Second Call.

12) One must take the number of the day of the drawing; if this does not exceed 10, then one combines it by adding together all the numbers of the 5 initial foundations <term>initial foundations: the primary numerical values established at the beginning of the calculation process</term>.

The number that arises from this is the second call <term>second call: the second predicted number for the lottery drawing</term>.

13) If, however, it exceeds 10, and the moon is not past the first quarter, one adds it to the age of the moon <note>The "age of the moon" refers to the number of days elapsed since the last new moon.</note>. This then gives the second call.

14) If it exceeds the tens <note>The original "10ner" refers to the value of ten.</note>, and the moon is in the 2nd or 3rd quarter, one adds to this the smaller half <note>In historical calculations, when an odd number was divided, the "smaller half" was the result rounded down (e.g., the smaller half of 9 is 4).</note> of the two aforementioned combined numbers. This then gives the second call.

15) If it exceeds two tens <note>original: "zwey 10ner," meaning the number 20.</note>, then one adds to it the planetary number of the year and the planetary number of the day, and adds them all together. This then gives the second call.

### How one should work out the Third Call.

19) One takes the number of the Solar Cycle <term>Solar Cycle: a 28-year chronological cycle used to determine which day of the week a particular date falls upon</term>, combines it with the number of the planet that rules on the day of the drawing <note>In historical astrology, each day of the week was ruled by one of the seven "classical" planets (e.g., Sunday by the Sun, Monday by the Moon).</note>; one multiplies this by 3, and combines the product with the number of the moon's age <note>The "moon's age" is the number of days since the last new moon.</note>, provided the moon is not yet past the half-way point of its course; this then gives the third call.

20) If the moon is already past the half-way point of its cycle, one subtracts 3 from this half as many times as possible; the remainder is then multiplied by 29 to obtain the third call <term>third call: the third predicted number in a lottery sequence</term>.

21) One takes the number of the Solar Cycle, the Golden Number <term>Golden Number: a value from 1 to 19 used to determine the lunar calendar and the date of Easter</term>, the number of the zodiac sign <note>German: *Himmelszeichen*</note> in which the moon is currently located, and the number of the drawing, adding them all together; if this resulting sum is odd <note>German: *ungleich*, literally "unequal," but used here to mean a number not divisible by two</note>, one takes the smaller half <note>meaning to divide by two and round down to the nearest whole number</note> and adds it to the previous number; if it is even, one combines it with its equal half <note>adding half of the value to itself</note>, and the number created through this process gives the third call.

22) Should it happen that the combination of these three numbers yields a total greater than 30, one multiplies them by 15; the result is then reduced algebraically <note>This likely refers to the numerological practice of "digital roots," where the digits of a large number are added together to find a smaller value</note>, and what remains is the third call.

If it should happen, however, that even after this reduction the number remains greater than 90, one proceeds according to the rules already prescribed above <note>The rules for the lottery typically required results between 1 and 90</note>.

## How to find the fourth call.

23) One takes the <term>Golden Number<note>A number from 1 to 19 used to track the moon's cycle over a 19-year period, essential for calculating dates like Easter.</note></term> and multiplies it by 4; to this, one adds the <term>lunar age<note>The number of days that have passed since the last New Moon.</note></term> likewise multiplied by 4; through this, one obtains the fourth call.

24) If the lunar age now exceeds one quarter, one further adds the lunar age multiplied by 3, and thereby obtains the fourth call.

25) But if the lunar age exceeds the second quarter, one adds the number of <term>solar degrees<note>The specific position of the sun within its current zodiac sign.</note></term> to the Golden Number and to the aforementioned lunar age; whatever results from this is the fourth call.

26) Furthermore, if the moon has exceeded three quarters by 2 or 3 days, one multiplies the number of its age and combines it with the Golden Number, and thereby obtains the fourth call.

27) When the moon has entered the last quarter, one takes the multiplied Golden Number, the entire lunar age, and also the number of the <term>sign<note>The astrological sign of the zodiac in which the moon is currently positioned.</note></term> in which the moon finds itself,

28) Furthermore, when the moon is completely at its end <note>This refers to the final days of the lunar cycle before a New Moon.</note>, one takes the <term>Golden Number<note>A value from 1 to 19 used to track the moon's cycle; essential for calculating movable feasts like Easter.</note></term> multiplied by 4; the <term>lunar age<note>The number of days that have passed since the last New Moon.</note></term> likewise multiplied by 4, and makes one sum from these two multiplied totals; this sum is multiplied anew by 29, the result is divided by 13, and what remains thereafter gives the fourth call.

If this number, however, exceeds 90 or 100, one proceeds with it as is stated in the rules given above.

### How the fifth call should be obtained.

29) One takes the number of the <term>epacts<note>The age of the moon in days on January 1st, used to synchronize the solar and lunar years.</note></term>, the number of the <term>Kalends<note>The first day of the month in the Roman calendar.</note></term>, the number of the age of the moon, and the number of the <term>sign of the sun<note>The specific zodiac sign in which the sun is currently positioned.</note></term>, sums them together, takes the larger half of that total (if it is an odd number), and adds it to the sum; thus one obtains the fifth call.

30) If the lunar age is more than 10, one multiplies it by 3 and adds this total to the numbers set above, and thereby obtains the fifth call.

31) When the <term>lunar age<note>The number of days that have passed since the last New Moon.</note></term> exceeds two tens <note>original: "Zehner"; meaning when the moon is 21 days or older.</note>, one multiplies it by 5 and combines the product with the numbers specified above; then, one multiplies this by 9 and divides it by 28, and the result gives the fifth call.

In chronology,
**epacts** <note>original: "Epacten." From the Greek *epaktos*, meaning "brought in" or "intercalated." It refers to the age of the moon in days on January 1st.</note> are the difference
of 11 days, which the
solar year <note>The time it takes for the Earth to orbit the sun, roughly 365 days.</note> has more than
the lunar year <note>A year based on twelve cycles of the moon's phases, roughly 354 days.</note>, because
the new moon goes back
11 days every year.
